item.title: Local mayors step up pressure to end border checks after crashes
item.description:
Local mayors step up pressure to end border checks after crashes

August 4, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The mayor of a border town has urged transport minister Vincent Karremans to hold talks with his German counterpart about border checkpoints following a string of serious accidents.

Four people have died in collisions near the border and at least 10 have suffered serious injuries since Germany reintroduced stricter checks in December 2024.

In the most recent incident last Friday, three people were injured in a crash involving four vehicles, including two lorries, on the A12 at Babberich, just before the border.

The German government has said it wants to extend the controls into the autumn, despite the implement of the European Migration Pact, which Dutch foreign minister David van Weel said would make the checkpoints “a thing of the past”.

Aad van Oosten, acting mayor of Zevenaar, urged Karremans to raise the issue with German interior minister Alexander Dobrint, who is a supporter of extending the controls.

“We have tried to raise awareness of our situation with other councils in the area, both in the Netherlands and Germany,” he told Omroep Gelderland. “All we get in reply is that there is no alternative.”

Chaos on roads

Van Oosten is not the first Dutch local politician to raise concerns about the impact of German border checks. In March Mark Boumans, mayor of Doetinchem, called for them to be scrapped following another five-vehicle collision, also at Babberich, in which three people were injured, including a child.

The following month Hubert Bruls, mayor of Nijmegen and chair of the council of Dutch regional safety boards, said the checks had cost millions of euros of damage and lost income and led to chaos on minor roads.

Bruls disputed the effectiveness of the checks after figures showed just under 3,500 people were suspected of trying to enter Germany illegally from the Netherlands and 1,750 were turned away at the border in six months.

Dutch officials checked the documents of 123,320 people at the border and turned 470 away in the first nine months after selected checks were introduced.

Van Oosten said the frequency of the accidents showed they could not be put down to inattentive motorists. “People should pay attention while driving, but this is a serious matter that is not as simple as just paying more attention,” he said.

item.title: Fourteen more councils placed under supervision over asylum
item.description:
Fourteen more councils placed under supervision over asylum

August 4, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Twenty-four councils are now under government supervision for failing to provide enough asylum accommodation, after asylum and migration minister Van den Brink added fourteen new names to the list.

His ministry publishes a monthly list of councils not meeting their legal obligation under the “spreading law”, which sets each council a share of the places the country needs. The first ten were named last month.

Being placed under supervision means the responsible councillors must come to the ministry to explain themselves and agree where and when an asylum centre will open.

The government uses a six-step escalation ladder. The 24 councils are on step three. At step six the cabinet can force a council to open a centre.

A ministry spokesperson said appearing on the list was a factual observation and doesn’t indicate a particular reason. It could reflect political unwillingness or other obstacles, which are established at talks with the ministry.

Only one of those talks has taken place so far, partly because of the summer holidays. That meeting was with Westland, which is required to house about 700 asylum seekers and has so far provided none. It has resisted the law for years, and its council previously said there was no local support for a centre.

The fourteen added are Aalsmeer, Bronckhorst, Brunssum, Bunschoten, De Ronde Venen, Dinkelland, Hardinxveld-Giessendam, Hellendoorn, Lopik, Montfoort, Oldebroek, Oldenzaal, Vlaardingen and Vught.

item.title: No plates, no fines: farmers escape penalty for A35 blockade
item.description:
No plates, no fines: farmers escape penalty for A35 blockade

August 4, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Around 80 farmers who blocked the A35 motorway near Almelo last Thursday will not be fined, because the number plates on their tractors were taped over and police cannot work out who they were.

Officers filmed the protest, but a police spokesman told regional broadcaster RTV Oost that the footage is unlikely to lead anywhere. “We have insufficient information,” he said.

Covering a number plate is itself an offence under Dutch traffic law, but police said that in this situation there is little they can do about it, given they cannot identify the drivers.

The blockade, on the stretch between Wierden and Almelo, lasted less than an hour but caused a four-kilometre jam. The farmers were protesting against the cabinet’s nitrogen emission plans.

Demonstrators told RTV Oost that they considered it a success and described it as a spur-of-the-moment action.

It is the latest in a series of tractor protests along Dutch roads this summer. Police took a different approach to a separate motorway blockade last month, arresting 270 Extinction Rebellion demonstrators who occupied the A12 in The Hague.

item.title: Readers still prefer paper books despite rise of digital options
item.description:
Readers still prefer paper books despite rise of digital options

August 4, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Paper books remain by far the most popular reading format despite the rise of e-readers and audiobooks, a study by ABN Amro has found.

Figures from Dutch publishers showed that physical books accounted for 86% of the total market in 2025, broadly in line with other countries such as the United States where paper books account for four-fifths of all sales.

The share of the total revenue is even larger because printed books are more expensive to produce, allowing for larger profit margins. E-books accounted for 6% of the total Dutch sales volume of €42 million.

The resilience of books at a time of advancing technology partly comes down to their simplicity: books do not need to be charged up, cannot crash or be deleted and can be replaced cheaply if necessary.

But books also have a prestige that makes them attractive to readers, ABN Amro wrote in a report titled “the paper book is still king”.

“Readers value the contact with paper, turning the page and even the smell of a book,” they said.

Status symbol

“A paper book is a possession that stands out from the bookcase, a sign of identity and status. So paper books are still attractive in a digital age because of the old-fashioned, analogue and direct character of the reading experience.”

Research at Tokyo University using MRI scanners found that reading on paper stimulates different processes in the brain from using a screen, promoting deeper understanding in readers and better retention of the information.

Nearly half of readers use paper books exclusively, while another 43% use a combination of printed, electronic and audio books. Only 2% listen exclusively to audiobooks, while another 5% only read e-books.

Lisa Kuitert, professor of book studies at the University of Amsterdam, said she was unsurprised by the findings.

“Ever since the emergence of digital books people have been saying the end of paper books is on its way. But people who say that aren’t readers,” she told the Financieele Dagblad. “People who enjoy reading prefer paper.”

Challenge of AI

ABN Amro said paper books were here to stay, but other formats were becoming increasingly important alternatives – particularly audiobooks, which people can listen to while on the move or exercising.

Mario Bersem, senior economist specialising in media and technology and one of the report’s authors, told Dutch News that bookshops still had a healthy future despite a sharp decline in the sector in the last 15 years.

“The number of bookshops has fallen hugely since 2010, but the drop was mainly at the start, when people started buying more from webshops. That shift seems to be behind us,” he said.

“Bookshops have become places to meet, much more than they used to be, where you can get a cup of coffee or attend a reading. But they are also still the main places where people buy books: 55% of books are sold over the counter.”

The report also said that an increasing number of published books are using AI for research, editing, translating or even producing texts. By one estimate, half of ebooks published in the United States in 2025 showed signs of AI use.

The use of AI has led to rows about authorial rights and compensation, as AI models are trained on published texts. In June Dutch publishers signed a “book pact” to protect authors from intellectual property theft and create a mechanism for paying royalties.

“For publishers AI clearly represents both an opportunity and a risk,” ABN Amro said in their report. “Technology can help with developing and distributing texts, but it can also put pressure on the value of intellectual property.”

item.title: Rabobank profit flat as it braces for loan losses
item.description:
Rabobank profit flat as it braces for loan losses

August 4, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Rabobank made no profit growth in the first half of this year, reporting a net profit of nearly €2.7 billion, the same as in the first six months of 2025, after setting aside €562 million for loans that might not be repaid.

That is more than four times the €136 million it set aside a year earlier, the bank said in its results statement.

Chairman Stefaan Decraene told reporters the provisions related to two cases in South America but declined to name the companies or projects involved, broadcaster NOS reported.

Business in the Netherlands grew. Deposits at the Dutch retail arm stood at €375.1 billion, and lending at €293 billion.

Takeover talk
Decraene said Rabobank was open to buying another bank, telling NOS that scale is becoming more important.

Rabobank also said it will invest up to €2 billion in strengthening its data and IT systems and scaling up its use of artificial intelligence. Reuters reported that the spending will be spread over the next three years.

The bank’s return on equity was 9.5% and its core capital ratio 20.2%, which it said makes it one of the best-capitalised banks in Europe.

item.title: Man who held prison staff hostage given suspended jail sentence
item.description:
Man who held prison staff hostage given suspended jail sentence

August 4, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A man who held three prison staff hostage at knifepoint for several hours has been given a further suspended sentence of a year.

Corné H. seized and handcuffed his victims for several hours on December 5 last year at the jail in Vught after threatening them and five other colleagues with kitchen knives.

The 30-year-old had served a nine-month term for holding four staff at a bar in Ede, Gelderland, against their will in March the previous year.

At the time of the incident he was being detained in Vught’s psychiatric unit waiting to be given a place in a clinic under the Dutch compulsory treatment system (tbs).

The sentence was suspended to allow H. to continue his treatment, which began in June, meaning he will only have to go back to prison if he commits another offence.

The court in Den Bosch heard that H. suffered as a result of conditions including PTSS, schizophrenia and autism, which influenced his behaviour. A psychiatric assessment also said he had “anti-social and borderline personality traits”.

The judge said his victims feared for their lives and the incident “must have been dreadful for them”, but accepted H. had diminished responsibility and imposed a sentence that met the prosecution service’s demands.

At the earlier trial, H. was cleared of taking the bar staff in Ede hostage but convicted of depriving them of their liberty and threatening them.

Police sealed off the venue after he went in at closing time with guns and explosives and threatened to blow up the building, leading to a stand-off lasting more than eight hours.

item.title: Police raise concerns over sharp rise in weapon seizures
item.description:
Police raise concerns over sharp rise in weapon seizures

August 4, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Dutch police seized 5,165 gas and alarm pistols, air weapons and pepper sprays last year, up from 4,080 in 2022, according to figures given to broadcaster NOS – a rise of almost 27%.

Police said they did not know whether the increase indicates that more people are carrying such weapons, or if it reflects boosted efforts to find and confiscate them.

Gas and alarm pistols are the main worry because they are hard to tell apart from real firearms, police spokesman Martin van der Meij told NOS. Alarm pistols make a loud bang but fire no projectile, while gas weapons can release tear gas.

They are cheap, easy to obtain and relatively simple to convert into working firearms, he said. A converted pistol was used to kill the crime reporter Peter R. de Vries in 2021.

Buying these weapons in Germany or Belgium and bringing them into the Netherlands is a criminal offence, though people do not always realise it.

Herman Oldenkotte, who runs a gun shop in Gronau just over the German border from Enschede, told NOS that he estimated 80% to 90% of his customers were Dutch. In Germany the weapons can be bought without a licence by anyone over 18.

Police also say more weapons are arriving by post. The Netherlands has pressed the EU for years to bring in a licence requirement or a ban.

Pepper spray is banned for civilians under Dutch weapons law. The justice ministry said in June it planned to allow permits for people at particular risk, such as stalking victims, while ruling out legalising it for everyone.

item.title: Limburg wildfire smoke reaches Friesland and Drenthe
item.description:
Limburg wildfire smoke reaches Friesland and Drenthe

August 4, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Smoke from the wildfire in northern Limburg is drifting as far north as Friesland and Drenthe, where emergency control rooms have been swamped with calls.

Safety authorities have asked people not to ring 112 unless they can actually see a fire, broadcaster NOS reported. The smell of the smoke has also been reported across Gelderland, including in Apeldoorn, Nijmegen and Doesburg, and across the German border in the Kleve district, according to German broadcaster WDR.

The fire, which started in the Boschhuizerbergen nature reserve near Oostrum, burned through at least 100 hectares, the Limburg-Noord emergency services authority said. A possible thunderstorm this evening could help quell the blaze.

An NL-Alert was sent out warning people to stay out of the smoke and close windows, doors and ventilation.

A spokesperson said that tackling the fire was tougher than expected and that wildfires can behave unpredictably.

Venray mayor Michiel Uitdehaag said firefighting would continue until at least 9am on Wednesday but that so far there had been no property damage or injuries. A nearby campsite was evacuated on Monday.

Two military helicopters are dropping water drawn from the Maas.

The fire started in dense woodland and sand drifts that fire engines cannot reach, NOS reported, and the wind keeps turning, sending the fire in different directions.

Not enough vehicles
The Dutch fire service does not have enough specialist wildfire vehicles because such fires are rare, Daan Peeters of the Nederweert brigade told NOS.

The vehicles being used at Venray were brought in from the centre of the country. Other fire services already have them, and more brigades should, he said, adding that the question was not when the next forest fire would come but where.

item.title: Police clear neighbourhood after explosives found in garden
item.description:
Police clear neighbourhood after explosives found in garden

August 4, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Bomb disposal specialists were called to a house in Rotterdam on Monday evening after a device was found during a police search.

Officers responded to reports of a person with a gun at the house in Voorne, in the Feijenoord district.

No weapons were found, but police cordoned off the area after explosives were found in the garden.

The disposal service EOD took the item away and destroyed it safely in the Kralingse Bos, Rotterdam’s largest urban park.

Police did not give any details of what the device was. Investigations are continuing.

item.title: Shell sells Dutch solar farms in retreat from renewables
item.description:
Shell sells Dutch solar farms in retreat from renewables

August 3, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Shell is selling every solar farm it owns in the Netherlands. The five sites, plus a combined wind and solar park at Pottendijk near Emmen, are going to the French oil company TotalEnergies.

The deal covers all of Shell’s wind and solar projects on land across Europe (its offshore windfarms are not included) and the company will not disclose what it is being paid.

The Dutch sites can produce up to 254 megawatts between them, enough to power tens of thousands of homes. They are at Moerdijk, Heerenveen, Emmen, and Sas van Gent and Koegorspolder near Terneuzen.

Some were built on land Shell had already used for oil and gas, and the company used them as proof it was changing. The Emmen farm stands on the site of an old gas treatment plant, part of a project Shell said could be an example for the rest of the country.

The sale needs approval from regulators and is expected to be completed at the end of 2026.

Retreating from transition
Wael Sawan, Shell’s chief executive, has shifted spending back towards oil and gas and away from low-carbon projects. TotalEnergies has moved the other way, buying renewable assets across Europe.

The Hague district court ordered Shell in 2021 to cut its emissions by 45% by 2030. The company dropped Royal Dutch from its name and moved its headquarters to London the following year, and won its appeal in November 2024.

Milieudefensie has taken that case to the Supreme Court and launched a second action last year over the company’s 700 oil and gas projects that are still in development.

Shell is not leaving Dutch renewable energy altogether. It keeps its stakes in North Sea wind farms, its Holland Hydrogen 1 plant at Rotterdam and its carbon capture work.
